prompt: On Android 15, the planner calls `notify` without holding `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. What does the student see, according to Google's documentation?
hint: The first two gates fail in silence.

choices.text: Nothing, and the app gets no error
choices.why: Right: the notification is dropped silently, which is why the app checks first.

choices.text: A crash with a `SecurityException` in the app
choices.why: Nothing is thrown; that silence is the problem.

choices.text: The permission dialog, shown automatically by the system
choices.why: For an app targeting 33 or later, asking is the app's job.

choices.text: The notification, but without sound
choices.why: Sound is the channel's importance; without the permission nothing arrives.

prompt: Put the gates in the order Android applies them to a notification the planner posts.
hint: The figure of section 02, left to right.
items: the app's notifications on in settings
the channel's importance decides how it arrives

prompt: Why can't this course show a screenshot of the planner's notification in the shade?

choices.text: Roborazzi only captures dark mode
choices.why: It captures whatever a composable draws, in either theme.

choices.text: The permission was never granted in the tests
choices.why: Section 04's test granted it and the notification was posted.

choices.text: Notifications are encrypted until shown
choices.why: Robolectric reads every field of them in the tests.

choices.text: The shade is the system's, not the app's
choices.why: Right: tests can ask what was posted, not photograph the system's screen.

prompt: What happens to a notification on Android 8.0 or later that names a channel id the app never created?

choices.text: The system creates the channel with default importance
choices.why: Only the app creates channels.

choices.text: It goes to a channel called `miscellaneous`
choices.why: That fallback does not exist for apps targeting 26 or later.

choices.text: The build fails with a missing-resource error
choices.why: Channel ids are strings checked at run time, not resources.

choices.text: It is not shown
choices.why: Right: a notification must belong to an existing channel.

prompt: The planner shipped its channel with importance 2. A new release creates the same channel id with importance 3. What do existing students get?
hint: After creation, importance belongs to the student.

choices.text: Importance 3, because the new code wins
choices.why: The system ignores the importance of an existing channel.

choices.text: Still 2
choices.why: Right: only the name and description are updated; a new id is the way out.

choices.text: A dialog asking whether to accept the change
choices.why: There is no such dialog.

choices.text: The channel is deleted and recreated at 3
choices.why: Nothing deletes it unless the app does so explicitly.

prompt: What importance number did the channel test print for the planner's `reminders` channel?
Why does the planner call `createChannels` in `PlannerApp.onCreate`, every time the process starts?
hint: What does creating an existing channel change?

choices.text: The system requires channels to be registered on every start
choices.why: Once is enough for the system; repeating is the app's convenience.

choices.text: To reset the importance the student changed
choices.why: It cannot: the student's choice wins.

choices.text: Channels are deleted each time the app closes
choices.why: Channels persist until the app deletes them or is uninstalled.

choices.text: Repeating it is harmless
choices.why: Right: an existing channel keeps the student's settings; only name and description refresh.

prompt: A colleague uses the full-colour launcher icon as the notification's small icon. What appears in the status bar?
hint: The system draws it in one colour from its shape.

choices.text: A solid square
choices.why: Right: every non-transparent pixel becomes the same colour.

choices.text: Nothing, because the build rejects colour icons for notifications
choices.why: The build accepts it; the result is just wrong.

choices.text: The app name in text
choices.why: The status bar shows an icon, not the name.

choices.text: The launcher icon, scaled down
choices.why: The colours are discarded; only the shape is used.

prompt: `showReminder` returns `true` or `false`. Why does it not simply return what `notify` returns?

choices.text: `notify` returns `Unit`, so it cannot say whether anything was shown
choices.why: Right: the answer has to come from checking first.

choices.text: `notify` throws when nothing is shown, and catching it is slow
choices.why: It throws nothing; it is silent.

choices.text: `notify` returns an id that is always positive
choices.why: It returns nothing at all.

choices.text: Returning booleans is required by lint
choices.why: Lint has no such rule; this is the app's design.

prompt: The notification removes itself from the shade when tapped because the builder calls `set___(true)`.
Why is the title built with `getString(R.string.reminder_title, courseName)` rather than `"$courseName today"`?

choices.text: Notifications refuse text that did not come from `strings.xml`
choices.why: Any `CharSequence` is accepted.

choices.text: `courseName` could contain a `$`
choices.why: A template inserts the value safely either way.

choices.text: String templates are slower than resources
choices.why: Speed is not the issue.

choices.text: Resources are translated; code is not
choices.why: Right: lesson 1 section 07's rule, applied to a notification.

prompt: The planner's manifest declares `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. On Android 15, does that let it post?

choices.text: No: the student still has to grant it in a dialog
choices.why: Right: the declaration only makes the permission askable.

choices.text: Yes, once Play Store review approves it
choices.why: The store does not grant runtime permissions.

choices.text: No, it is reserved for system apps
choices.why: Any app can ask for it.

choices.text: Yes, declaring is granting
choices.why: That was true of install-time permissions, not of this one.

prompt: Match each situation from section 05 to what `canNotify` answered.
hint: Two of them are `false` for different reasons.

pairs.right: false, and the app can still ask

pairs.left: API 35, granted, switched off in settings
pairs.right: false, and asking again is not possible
true, because the permission does not exist there

right_distractors: true, because the manifest declares it

prompt: In Robolectric, a test that calls `notify` without the permission on API 35 sees one notification posted. What should you conclude?
hint: A stand-in is not the rule.

choices.text: That `targetSdk` must be lowered to 32
choices.why: Lowering it would hide the problem from the test and from nobody else.

choices.text: That Android 15 lets apps post without asking
choices.why: Google's documentation says the opposite; Robolectric simply does not enforce it.

choices.text: Robolectric does not enforce it
choices.why: Right: a test of code that skipped the check would pass, and students would see nothing.

choices.text: That `@SuppressLint` grants the permission
choices.why: It silences a warning and changes nothing at run time.

prompt: Why does `canNotify` test `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33` before checking the permission?
hint: Below 33 the permission is not defined.

choices.text: So that lint stops warning about `notify`
choices.why: The `@SuppressLint` handles the warning.

choices.text: To make the app refuse to run on Android 12
choices.why: It runs, and posts, on Android 12.

choices.text: To state in code that older phones need no permission
choices.why: Right: the planner then does not depend on what `checkSelfPermission` answers for an undefined permission.

choices.text: Because `checkSelfPermission` crashes below 33
choices.why: It answered without crashing in the Android 12 test.

prompt: What happens on Android 12 or later if the planner creates its `PendingIntent` with neither `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` nor `FLAG_MUTABLE`?

choices.text: It throws an `IllegalArgumentException`
choices.why: Right: since Android 12 every `PendingIntent` must say which it is.

choices.text: The tap does nothing
choices.why: It never gets that far; creation fails.

choices.text: Lint fails the build
choices.why: The failure is at run time.

choices.text: It defaults to mutable
choices.why: There is no default any more; the call fails.

prompt: A colleague gives every reminder's `PendingIntent` request code 0, with `FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT`. Reminders for Kotlin and SQL are both in the shade. What does tapping Kotlin's do?
hint: Two intents that differ only in extras are the same `PendingIntent`.

choices.text: Opens Kotlin, as intended
choices.why: Both share one `PendingIntent`, updated by the last post.

choices.text: Opens the course posted last, SQL
choices.why: Right: the extras were updated to SQL's, for both notifications.

choices.text: Crashes, because two notifications share an intent
choices.why: Sharing is allowed; it is just wrong here.

choices.text: Opens nothing until the app restarts
choices.why: The tap works; it opens the wrong course.

prompt: `ReplaceTest` posted three reminders for two courses. How many notifications were in the shade?
Why is `courseId.hashCode()` a convenient notification id and not a guaranteed one?

choices.text: Notification ids must be below 1000
choices.why: Any `Int` is accepted.

choices.text: A negative hash code is refused by `notify`
choices.why: Negative ids work.

choices.text: Hash codes change on every run
choices.why: A `String`'s `hashCode` is fixed by its characters.

choices.text: Two ids could share one
choices.why: Right: with three courses the risk is negligible; with thousands, a real integer id is safer.

prompt: Where do most students ever read the name and description you gave the planner's channel?

choices.text: In the app's notification settings
choices.why: Right: that is where the student turns a channel up, down or off.

choices.text: In the Play Store listing
choices.why: Channels are not listed there.

choices.text: In the permission dialog
choices.why: The dialog names the app, not its channels.

choices.text: In the notification itself
choices.why: The notification shows the title and text, not the channel.

prompt: The student's phone is in Do Not Disturb when the planner posts a reminder on its default-importance channel. What should the planner do about it?

choices.text: Raise the channel to high importance so it breaks through
choices.why: Apps cannot raise an existing channel, and should not try here.

choices.text: Nothing: a silent reminder in the shade is right
choices.why: Right: a study reminder should not interrupt somebody who asked not to be.

choices.text: Post it again every minute until it is seen
choices.why: That replaces the same notification and teaches the student to switch the channel off.

choices.text: Ask for a Do Not Disturb permission at start-up
choices.why: Overriding the student's choice is exactly what section 07 rejects.

prompt: Which of these make a posted reminder fail to reach the student, with no error in the app? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three gates, and one of them is the channel.

choices.text: The phone is in Do Not Disturb
choices.why: No: it still reaches the shade, silently.

choices.text: Android 14, permission never granted
choices.why: Yes: the first gate.

choices.text: The student switched the `reminders` channel off
choices.why: Yes: importance none blocks it.

choices.text: Android 11, nothing ever asked
choices.why: No: before Android 13 there is no permission to hold.

prompt: `canNotify` returns `false` on an Android 15 phone. Before deciding to ask for the permission, what else must the planner find out?

choices.text: Whether the channel has been created yet
choices.why: `canNotify` does not look at channels.

choices.text: Whether the phone is in Do Not Disturb
choices.why: Do Not Disturb does not make `canNotify` false.

choices.text: Whether `targetSdk` is 36
choices.why: That is fixed at build time and the same on every phone.

choices.text: Which of `false`'s two causes applies
choices.why: Right: only the first can be asked for; the second is the student's decision in settings.
